# The machine bancada runs on registers itself

> The product is already executing there, so its prefix, path mapping and filesystem access are facts rather than claims — and asking a person to write them down is asking them to restate one.

Applies to `crates/bancada-core/**`, `app/src-tauri/src/commands/**`.

<!-- archwarden:yours -->

## Context

_Everything between these two markers is yours. archwarden never rewrites it._

<!-- archwarden:end -->

## Considered and rejected

- **Requiring the local machine to be registered like any other runtime** (nothing refuses it) — Made the first five minutes absurd: describing your own laptop in JSON, every field of which the product could only have gotten right.
- **Persisting the synthesised runtime into the configuration file** (nothing refuses it) — Freezes today's `$HOME` into a file that outlives it, and the copy on disk quietly wins over the fact.
- **A default that cannot be overridden** (nothing refuses it) — A default that cannot be overridden is one that eventually lies. An entry somebody edited no longer equals the default and survives.

## What keeps it

Nothing can. It is behaviour at read time: a runtime synthesised before validation and dropped before writing. Nothing in the file layout shows it.
